FRENCH — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.

2. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. livre
   B. porte
   C. chaise
   D. fenêtre

3. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.

4. When practising Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.

5. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me
   B. Good night only
   C. Good morning / hello
   D. Thank you

6. When practising Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.

7. When practising Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.

8. When practising Active listening 1.4 Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.

9. When practising Interactive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Listening.

10. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Interactive Speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Interactive Speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading aloud 2.2 Reading for understanding 2.2 Guided reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Guided reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Aloud Tone Clarity Voice projection and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
